items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: And playing with Joe Wilder, you know, he’s played with all the greats. And last night he would call tunes... I enjoyed your set last night with Joe Wilder.

ctx.x: It was. What’s it like to fit in in a band that obviously is not rehearsed? Do you feel comfortable with having the repertoire under your belt for these kinds of things?

Well that always helps. It always helps to be familiar with a wide range of the jazz repertoire. And you never know, you’re kind of taken out of your comfort zone when you’re at a jazz party and they throw a bunch of different guys together and say okay we’re going to try this. Because you find comfort when you play with the same guys all the time, you know what they’re going to do, they know how to interact with what it is © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

that you’re going play, and then they say okay. So it’s a bunch of guys that you might have played with here, there, maybe a jam session. But all in all I think that it’s a good thing, it’s a good experience. It keeps you on your toes. And playing with Joe Wilder, you know, he’s played with all the greats. And last night he would call tunes, and I knew most of them but there were a couple of tunes that he was calling that not everyone was familiar with.
